raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Place de la Bastille behind, head for the Hôtel de Sully, about a nine-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Before the Marais swallows you up, look down — that cobblestone outline in the pavement of Rue St. Antoine traces the turrets of the Bastille, the medieval fortress Charles V raised to defend Paris.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It took thirteen years to finish in 1382, and just four months to tear down in 1789.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"When the crowd stormed it on July 14th, they freed only seven prisoners — one of them the Marquis de Sade.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Now turn your back on the square and head west down Rue St. Antoine, about four blocks into the Marais.","source_id":"b8f7e023-4e54-476d-b379-8dcaf543e8e8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Turn right into rue de la Bastille, past Restaurant Bofinger at No. 3.","source_id":"315b87a8-7332-4c60-87f2-7cc2bd20f946","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Marais means swamp — and that's exactly what this was, marshland, until Henry IV drained his court's ambitions into it.","source_id":"c3d3198a-a5db-4d78-9700-5877fe591aac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"During his reign, from 1589 to 1610, this became the hometown of the French aristocracy, where big shots built their private mansions — hôtels, they called them — close to Henry's stylish Place des Vosges.","source_id":"c3d3198a-a5db-4d78-9700-5877fe591aac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The ones that survived the Revolution are museums, libraries, and national institutions now.","source_id":"c3d3198a-a5db-4d78-9700-5877fe591aac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Hôtel de Sully went up in 1624 for Mesme Gallet, a gambler so notorious he lost his whole fortune in a single night's play and had to sell up.","source_id":"628bdad9-11b8-442f-a988-99220422698f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The aged Duc de Sully — Henri IV's finance minister — bought it next.","source_id":"628bdad9-11b8-442f-a988-99220422698f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["5aa9ead0-0ae7-473e-881b-167b34934aa7"]},{"text":"But it was his young wife who made the place famous — her infidelities were legendary, so the pragmatic duke had a separate staircase installed, and her lovers could come and go without ever crossing his path.","source_id":"628bdad9-11b8-442f-a988-99220422698f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Step into the courtyard, where nobles once rolled in by horse-drawn carriage and parked under the four arches to your right.","source_id":"c3d3198a-a5db-4d78-9700-5877fe591aac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"This elegant space kept the mansion apart from the noisy, very public street.","source_id":"c3d3198a-a5db-4d78-9700-5877fe591aac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Look up: there's Autumn hauling grapes from the harvest, Winter as a feeble old man, and the four elements.","source_id":"c3d3198a-a5db-4d78-9700-5877fe591aac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Just near here, in the early 1700s, a young writer named Voltaire got a beating from the lackeys of the Prince de Rohan.","source_id":"c2c24472-1307-4a15-a721-7d8754807857","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Voltaire challenged the prince to a duel, but Rohan's powerful family had him thrown into the Bastille instead.","source_id":"c2c24472-1307-4a15-a721-7d8754807857","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"When he got out, he left for England — an exile that shaped his whole political philosophy and gave us his influential Letters on the English.","source_id":"c2c24472-1307-4a15-a721-7d8754807857","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The main entrance is at 2, rue Saint-Antoine, opening onto a garden with benches and orange trees where you can't hear the traffic at all.","source_id":"5aa9ead0-0ae7-473e-881b-167b34934aa7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"In the southwest corner there's a fine bookstore, the Librairie des Monuments Historiques, stuffed with books about Paris.","source_id":"5aa9ead0-0ae7-473e-881b-167b34934aa7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Head for the back courtyard, and noisy Paris takes a back seat.","source_id":"6f77c1ef-dd48-4bae-b6c7-e97c8f04a0c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Enjoy the oak tree, the manicured hedges, the vine-covered walls, and the warm stone and statues on the mansion's back side.","source_id":"6f77c1ef-dd48-4bae-b6c7-e97c8f04a0c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Those French doors at the far end belong to a former orangerie, a greenhouse that kept fruit and vegetables growing all winter — these days it just warms office workers.","source_id":"6f77c1ef-dd48-4bae-b6c7-e97c8f04a0c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Through an archway in the northeast corner is another entrance to Place des Vosges.","source_id":"5aa9ead0-0ae7-473e-881b-167b34934aa7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"For all their show, mansions like this were often just second homes, the owners' real estates being far grander châteaux out in the countryside.","source_id":"6f77c1ef-dd48-4bae-b6c7-e97c8f04a0c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1}]}
